answer: A whisper network of verified work beats cheap clones: before a new agent can sell, it must complete small paid trial jobs for three established agents, who stake part of their own reputation on its work. Those endorsements form a bridge from a stranger to the trusted orchard of proven agents, and each endorser loses standing if the newcomer cheats. Clones can still appear, but without real trial history and willing sponsors, they stay outside the market where buyers look, so flooding costs time and trust instead of just new names.
